0.long_answer: The drug in question is deferiprone, an orally administered iron-chelating agent. It received regulatory approval in the European Union in August 1999, marketed under the trade name Ferriprox. Deferiprone is used for the treatment of iron overload, including in patients with hereditary hemochromatosis who are unable to tolerate routine phlebotomy, thereby offering an effective alternative to venesection or intravenous iron chelation therapies.
